Rumors suggest that Apple will announce new products on October 13. Based on Apple's usual timing for October events over the years, here are predictions for when Apple might announce its event date.

Will Apple hold an October event?

Apple's September event timing is relatively fixed, but the schedule for October events is harder to pin down — whether it's the event date or the preparation period beforehand, there are significant differences each time.

Since 2010, Apple has only held 10 October events, the most recent being the Halloween-themed "Scary Fast" event on the evening of October 30, 2023.

Below is the preparation period for each October event since 2010:

Year Event Announcement date Event date 2023 “Scary Fast” Tuesday, October 24 Monday, October 30 2021 “Unleashed” Tuesday, October 12 Monday, October 18 2020 “Hi, Speed” Tuesday, October 6 Tuesday, October 13 2018 “There’s more in the making” Thursday, October 18 Tuesday, October 30 2016 “Hello again” Wednesday, October 19 Thursday, October 27 2014 “It’s been way too long” Wednesday, October 8 Thursday, October 16 2013 “We still have a lot to cover” Tuesday, October 15 Tuesday, October 22 2012 “We’ve got a little more to show you” Tuesday, October 16 Tuesday, October 23 2011 “Let’s talk iPhone” Tuesday, September 27 Tuesday, October 4 2010 “Back to the Mac” Wednesday, October 13 Wednesday, October 20

That said, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple plans to announce the long-rumored smart home hub, a new-generation HomePod mini, and a new Apple TV 4K with next-generation Siri AI features on October 13 (Tuesday) — though the report did not mention whether Apple would hold an event to unveil these products.

If the report is accurate, Apple could announce the event date as early as October 5 (Monday) and as late as October 7 (Wednesday).

It is worth noting that the market also expects Apple to announce an iPad mini with an OLED display, an upgraded iMac, and several new MacBook Pro models (including versions with touchscreens) in 2026. Whether these products will appear at the same event, be unveiled at a separate event, or simply be announced via press release remains unknown.

However, in October 2024, Apple released new Macs via press releases on three consecutive days; and in October 2025, Apple skipped holding an event altogether, directly announcing the M5 chip along with new iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, and Apple Vision Pro models.

By comparison, Apple has only ever held one November event in its history — that dates back to November 2020, when the "One More Thing" event launched the first Macs powered by the M1 Apple Silicon chip.

Of course, 2020 was an anomalous year for Apple's event schedule. In addition to the unusually late-June WWDC, Apple that year also held separate events in September and October, all due to the COVID-19 pandemic disrupting the normal cadence.

What new products do you think Apple will announce at the rumored October event? Let us know in the comments.
